contests.title: Clear Creek County Ballot Issue 1A — Lodging Tax Revenue: Additional Allowable Uses and Allocations
contests.scopeNote: Registered electors in Clear Creek County outside the Town of Georgetown, as expressly specified by Resolution R-26-55.

provenance.quote: SHALL CLEAR CREEK COUNTY LODGING TAXES BE INCREASED BY $800,000.00 ANNUALLY COMMENCING ON JANUARY 1, 2027, AND BY WHATEVER AMOUNTS ARE RAISED ANNUALLY THEREAFTER, BY INCREASING THE LODGING TAX RATE FROM TWO PERCENT (2%) TO SIX PERCENT (6%) ON THE RENTAL FEE, PRICE, OR OTHER CONSIDERATION PAID OR CHARGED FOR THE LEASING, RENTAL, SALE OR FURNISHING OF A ROOM OR ACCOMMODATION FOR A SHORT-TERM PERIOD OF LESS THAN THIRTY (30) CONSECUTIVE DAYS IN CLEAR CREEK COUNTY, EXCLUDING THE MUNICIPALITY OF THE TOWN OF GEORGETOWN THAT CURRENTLY HAS ITS OWN ADOPTED LODGING TAX, AND SHALL THE ALLOCATION OF COUNTY LODGING TAX REVENUE BE MODIFIED SO THAT THE REVENUE COLLECTED FROM THE SIX PERCENT (6%) COUNTY LODGING TAX SHALL BE USED AS FOLLOWS: • UP TO 60% OF THE REVENUE FOR PUBLIC INFRASTRUCTURE MAINTENANCE OR IMPROVEMENTS; AND ENHANCING PUBLIC SAFETY MEASURES; • AT LEAST TWENTY PERCENT (20%) OF THE REVENUE TO PROVIDE CHILDCARE FOR THE TOURISM-RELATED WORKFORCE, INCLUDING SEASONAL WORKERS, AND FOR OTHER WORKERS IN THE COMMUNITY; • AT LEAST TEN PERCENT (10%) OF THE REVENUE TO PROVIDE HOUSING FOR THE TOURISM-RELATED WORKFORCE, INCLUDING SEASONAL WORKERS, AND FOR OTHER WORKERS IN THE COMMUNITY; • AT LEAST TEN PERCENT (10%) OF THE REVENUE FOR ADVERTISING AND MARKETING OF LOCAL TOURISM, AS REQUIRED BY STATE LAW; AND WITH ALL SUCH EXPENDITURES SUBJECT TO AN ANNUAL INDEPENDENT AUDIT AND SPENT IN COMPLIANCE WITH LOCAL GOVERNMENT BUDGET LAWS, AND SHALL THE FIRST-YEAR REVENUE, AND WHATEVER ADDITIONAL AMOUNTS ARE RAISED ANNUALLY THEREAFTER, BE COLLECTED AND SPENT AS A VOTER APPROVED REVENUE CHANGE NOTWITHSTANDING ANY LIMITATION OR CONDITION UNDER ARTICLE X, SECTION 20 OF THE COLORADO CONSTITUTION OR ANY OTHER PROVISION OF LAW?
provenance.sourceOrg: Clear Creek County Board of County Commissioners

contests.title: Montezuma County Lodging Tax Ballot Issue 1B
contests.scopeNote: Registered electors in Montezuma County outside the City of Cortez. Current county lodging question excludes Cortez; the official Cortez sample omits it, consistent with C.R.S.§30-11-107.5(3).

provenance.quote: SHALL MONTEZUMA COUNTY LODGING TAXES BE INCREASED BY $404,598 IN TAX COLLECTION YEAR 2027 AND BY WHATEVER AMOUNTS ARE GENERATED ANNUALLY THEREAFTER BY INCREASING THE COUNTY LODGING TAX FROM 2% TO 5% EFFECTIVE JANUARY 1, 2027, EXCLUDING THE MUNICIPALITY OF CORTEZ WHICH HAS ITS OWN LODGING TAX, AND SHALL THE LODGING TAX REVENUES RECEIVED BY THE COUNTY BE USED FOR THE FOLLOWING PURPOSES: • TOURISM PROMOTION AND MARKETING; • RECREATION, OUTDOOR RECREATION, AND VISITOR-RELATED INFRASTRUCTURE IMPROVEMENTS; • DESTINATION DEVELOPMENT PROJECTS AND VISITOR EXPERIENCE ENHANCEMENTS; • TOURISM RESILIENCY, EMERGENCY RESPONSE, AND RECOVERY EFFORTS RELATED TO EVENTS AFFECTING VISITATION; • ADMINISTRATION, OVERSIGHT, AND IMPLEMENTATION OF AUTHORIZED LODGING TAX PROGRAMS; AND SHALL THE COUNTY BE AUTHORIZED TO COLLECT, RETAIN, AND SPEND ALL REVENUES GENERATED BY SUCH TAX AS A VOTER- APPROVED REVENUE CHANGE UNDER ARTICLE X, SECTION 20 OF THE COLORADO CONSTITUTION, OR ANY OTHER LAW?

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Increase the county lodging tax from 2% to 6% for paid lodging stays shorter than 30 consecutive days beginning January 1, 2027. Georgetown is excluded because it has its own lodging tax. The question authorizes $800,000 annually starting in 2027 and whatever amounts are raised in later years, with no stated end date. It also changes how revenue from the full 6% tax would be allocated, as described below. All spending would be subject to an annual independent audit and local government budget laws. Tax revenue could be collected and spent outside the stated constitutional and other legal limits.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the lodging-tax increase, the new allocations for all revenue from the 6% tax, the annual audit requirement and its revenue-limit exception.
measureRecords.noMeans: Do not approve this lodging-tax increase, allocation change or proposed revenue-limit exception.

parts.label: How the revenue would be divided
parts.what: Up to 60% would go to public infrastructure maintenance or improvements and public-safety measures combined. At least 20% would go to childcare, at least 10% to housing, and at least 10% to advertising and marketing local tourism. Childcare and housing could serve tourism-related workers, including seasonal workers, and other workers in the community.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Increase the county lodging tax from 2% to 5% beginning January 1, 2027, excluding Cortez, which has its own lodging tax. The question authorizes $404,598 in additional taxes in 2027 and whatever amounts the tax generates later, with no stated end date. Uses would include tourism promotion; recreation and visitor-related infrastructure; destination development and visitor-experience projects; tourism resiliency, emergency response and recovery related to events affecting visits; and administering and overseeing authorized lodging-tax programs. All revenue generated by the tax could be collected, retained and spent outside the stated constitutional and other legal limits.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the county lodging-tax increase outside Cortez for the stated purposes and its revenue-limit exception.
measureRecords.noMeans: Do not approve this county lodging-tax increase or its proposed revenue-limit exception.
